::: {.why}
Your definition from last night is probably a number per stock per day, which is right and incomplete, because the missing part is what the number's units are and that decides everything downstream.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the interface a signal must satisfy: what it takes, what it returns, and what its units are.
- Say what changes when a signal is a forecast of return, a forecast of rank, and an arbitrary score.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Write the interface in qlib/signals/base.py: a signal takes an as-of date and a universe and returns one number per security, with the units declared as an attribute. Requiring the units to be declared is the point; a score with undeclared units cannot be combined with another one honestly.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Port the two things you already have to it: the pairs spread z-score and the trend follower's position, both expressed as signals rather than as positions. Then note what you had to decide to do it, which is the sizing rule you had previously buried in each strategy.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the three unit conventions and their consequences into reports/milestone-06-alpha-book.md, since week 29 combines signals and cannot do it without them.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
qlib/signals/base.py defines the signal interface for the whole alpha book: as-of date in, one score per security out, units declared. The two existing strategies become signals, which separates the forecast from the sizing for the first time.
:::
